text: Let X be a Banach space and let f belong to L1(0,T;X). The function f has an integrable weak derivative g if and only if there is a constant c0 such that f(t)=c0+integral_0^t g(s) ds for almost every t. In this case the strong derivative exists almost everywhere and agrees with g.

source.locator: Section 6.A.3, Theorem 6.35, printed p.203 (PDF p.209), equation (6.43)

scope: Banach-valued functions with an integrable weak derivative on a finite interval; the source concludes almost-everywhere differentiability.
